findings.title: Path Traversal Open
findings.description: The current implementation is vulnerable to path traversal attacks because it only strips the directory path using os.path.basename, but does not prevent attacks using relative paths like '..' or '.'. A more robust approach is to validate the filename against a whitelist or use a library like pathlib to handle path manipulation. By adding additional validation, we can prevent unauthorized access to files outside the intended directory.
findings.cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
findings.fix_hint: Validate and sanitize the filename to prevent path traversal attacks by using a whitelist approach or a library like pathlib
findings.fixed_code: filename = os.path.basename(filename); if not filename or '..' in filename or '/' in filename or '\' in filename: return 'Invalid filename'; with open(os.path.join('/var/data', filename)) as f: return f.read()

findings.title: Security group allows unrestricted SSH (port 22)
findings.description: The security group allows unrestricted access to port 22, which is a critical vulnerability. To fix this, we need to restrict the ingress rule to only allow SSH access from trusted IP addresses or CIDR blocks. By updating the security group resource, we can limit the exposure to only trusted sources.
findings.fix_hint: Restrict the security group to only allow SSH access from trusted IP addresses or CIDR blocks

findings.title: Aws Db Instance No Logging
findings.description: The AWS DB instance is missing logging configuration, which can cause important event information to be lost. Enabling logging by setting 'enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports' will allow the instance to export logs to CloudWatch. This will provide visibility into database events and help with auditing and troubleshooting.
findings.cwe: CWE-311: Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data
findings.fix_hint: Enable logging for the AWS DB instance by setting the 'enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports' argument
findings.fixed_code:
resource "aws_db_instance" "app_db" {
  identifier          = "app-db"
  engine              = "mysql"
  instance_class      = "db.t3.micro"
  username            = "admin"
  password            = var.db_password
  publicly_accessible = false
  storage_encrypted   = true
  enabled_cloudwatch_logs_exports = ["error", "general", "slowquery"]
}

findings.description: S3 versioning allows for the storage of multiple versions of an object in the same bucket, enabling easy recovery from accidental deletion or overwrite. This can be fixed by adding the 'deletion_protection' argument to the 'aws_db_instance' resource and setting it to 'true'
findings.fix_hint: Enable deletion protection for the AWS DB instance to prevent accidental deletion

findings.fix_hint: Remove or restrict the overly permissive ec2 actions in the policy

The provided fixed code maintains the same level of access, but it is essential to review and ensure that these actions are indeed necessary for the application's functionality.

attack_chains.title: EC2 Public IP and Unrestricted SSH
attack_chains.description: An attacker can gain access to the EC2 instance using the public IP and unrestricted SSH, allowing them to execute arbitrary commands and access sensitive data. This can lead to a full system compromise and data exfiltration. The attacker can then use the instance as a pivot point to attack other resources in the cloud environment.
steps: Step 1: attacker gains access to the EC2 instance using the public IP (finding c51a5a50 in file xentinel-test-v3/infra/main.tf)
Step 2: attacker uses the unrestricted SSH (finding 3c9d1f3f in file xentinel-test-v3/infra/main.tf) to execute arbitrary commands and access sensitive data
attack_chains.remediation: Restrict SSH access to the EC2 instance by updating the security group to only allow incoming SSH connections from trusted IP addresses.

attack_chains.title: Path Traversal and Unrestricted S3 Access
attack_chains.description: An attacker can use the path traversal vulnerability to access sensitive data on the S3 bucket, and then use the unrestricted S3 access to exfiltrate the data. This can lead to a significant data breach and compromise of sensitive information. The attacker can then use the exfiltrated data to launch further attacks on the organization.
steps: Step 1: attacker uses the path traversal vulnerability (finding bb0d479c in file src/app.py) to access sensitive data on the S3 bucket
Step 2: attacker uses the unrestricted S3 access (finding efab4cc2 in file iam/policy.json) to exfiltrate the sensitive data
attack_chains.remediation: Update the S3 bucket policy to restrict access to only trusted IP addresses and users, and patch the path traversal vulnerability in the application code.

attack_chains.title: EC2 Public IP and Dangerous IAM Action
attack_chains.description: An attacker can use the public IP of the EC2 instance to gain access to the instance, and then use the dangerous IAM action to escalate privileges and access sensitive data. This can lead to a full system compromise and data exfiltration. The attacker can then use the instance as a pivot point to attack other resources in the cloud environment.
steps: Step 1: attacker gains access to the EC2 instance using the public IP (finding c51a5a50 in file xentinel-test-v3/infra/main.tf)
Step 2: attacker uses the dangerous IAM action (finding 4fe7943e in file iam/policy.json) to escalate privileges and access sensitive data
attack_chains.remediation: Restrict the IAM action to only allow necessary privileges, and update the EC2 instance to use a private IP address instead of a public IP.
